page: Hetzner Cloud cax11 is an entry-level, Arm64-based virtual server belonging to the cax family, running on the QEMU hypervisor. It features 2 shared vCPUs powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, with 2 physical cores and a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 40 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the cax11 demonstrates modest performance characteristics typical of shared-core Arm configurations. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is rated as average with a score of 1821.28, but multi-core performance drops to the weak tier at 3610.67. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor throughput, with read-only large block speeds at 25.88 GB/sec and write speeds at 15.72 GB/sec. Computational benchmarks, such as Geekbench (single-core score of 1014.0 and multi-core score of 1826.0) and Passmark (CPU score of 1579.57), place the server in the lower performance tiers. Database operations and Redis SET performance (2.58 million operations per second) are also categorized as weak.

Given its shared CPU allocation and lower-tier benchmark results, the cax11 represents a highly cost-efficient option for resource-light applications where continuous high-performance CPU utilization is not required. The inclusion of 40 GB NVMe SSD storage provides fast local I/O relative to the low resource density. This server is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, development and testing environments, small-scale Redis caching, and simple background task processing. It is not recommended for intensive database operations, multi-threaded compilation, or machine learning workloads.
